## Things to check before shipping

These are worth knowing about. They don't require changing the plan.

1. **The description controls when the skill loads.** Claude decides whether to use a skill based mostly on its description. "Anything related to our company" is too vague to match reliably. Some prompts that should trigger it won't, like "why is the `queue-lag` alert firing?" Others that shouldn't, will. A more specific one-liner takes no extra effort:
   > `description: Company handbook covering Python/TypeScript code style, deploy and rollback steps for our 4 services, on-call alert runbook, PTO/expense policy, brand voice for marketing copy, org chart, and internal glossary. Use when writing code, deploying, handling alerts, answering policy questions, writing marketing copy, or looking up people or internal terms.`

2. **All 3,000 lines load at once.** When the skill triggers, the whole SKILL.md enters context. A question about the expense policy would also pull in 900 lines of runbook. That costs tokens and can make answers worse. You can fix this and still have one skill. Keep a short SKILL.md that serves as an index, and put each section in its own file in the same folder, e.g. `runbook.md` and `code-style.md`. SKILL.md then just says "for alerts, read `runbook.md`." It's still one skill and one folder, and each section is easier to edit.

3. **Phone numbers in the org chart.** Putting personal phone numbers into a file that's shared and loaded into model context could be a privacy or policy problem. Check with whoever owns that data. Names and roles alone may be enough.

If you go with the paste-it-all version today, swapping in the description from #1 is the highest-value change and costs nothing.
